under-construction.name: M2 western extension (under construction)
under-construction.description: Three more stations west of Bemowo, Lazurowa, Chrzanów and Karolin, with the line's second depot at Karolin; under construction since 2021, due to open in 2026–2027.

m1-infill.name: Plac Konstytucji and Muranów
m1-infill.description: Two M1 stations planned in the 1980s and dropped in 1989 to save money, leaving gaps between Politechnika and Centrum and between Ratusz Arsenał and Dworzec Gdański; a design tender was announced in 2019 and the 2023 plan keeps them.

m3-first-stage.name: M3, first stage
m3-first-stage.description: A third line from the spare platform at Stadion Narodowy, built in 2015 for it, to Gocław through Grochów, with a depot at Kozia Górka; approved in 2021, in design since 2024, construction planned from 2028.

five-lines-2050.name: Five metro lines by 2050
five-lines-2050.description: The city's February 2023 plan: M1's two missing stations, M2 extended to Ursus and from Bródno under the Vistula to Marymont, M3 on from Gocław under the river to Żwirki i Wigury, and two new lines, M4 (Tarchomin–Wilanów, stations as designed in 2026) and M5 (Ursus–Gocławek); M4 is in design, the rest are studies, all meant to be built by about 2048.

deep-metro-1950s.name: Deep metro (1950–1957)
deep-metro-1950s.description: A Y-shaped deep-level line decided in 1950, from Plac Komuny Paryskiej (Plac Wilsona) to Plac Unii Lubelskiej with a branch from ul. Próżna under the Vistula to Dworzec Wileński and a depot at Targówek. Work began on the Praga side in 1951, was cut back to a trial section in 1953 and stopped in 1957, leaving a 1.3 km tunnel near ul. Radzymińska.

metropolitan-1927.name: Metropolitan (1927–1939)
metropolitan-1927.description: The city's pre-war underground: a north–south line from Plac Wilsona to Plac Unii Lubelskiej and an east–west line from ul. Wolska under the Vistula to Dworzec Wschodni, approved in 1927 and revised from 1938, within a seven-line network to be built over 35 years; preparatory work stopped when the war broke out.
